label: GO after a2 S2 unrewarded, grows late in episode, after repeated losses, moderate a2 policy
terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * np.clip(ep_trial - 40, 0, 60) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * np.clip(ep_trial - 40, 0, 60) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * np.clip(ep_trial - 40, 0, 60) * (choice < 0) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * np.clip(ep_trial - 40, 0, 60) * np.clip(-choice, 0, 5)
explanation: Sparse feature (0.9% of steps). It fires only at GO, and almost only after a common-unrewarded a2 trial (a2 -> S2, no reward); D1 and D2 are always zero. Its magnitude rises roughly linearly with episode trial after about trial 40. It is larger when the trial before was also unrewarded (two losses in a row on a2, e.g. 0.45 vs 0.3), and larger when the policy still leans a2 (choice < 0), but only moderately: the strongest-a2 logits give less, and it is near zero once the agent is about to switch to a1. Other previous-trial patterns, value, the hidden good state and reward-x-state give nothing. Scores (R^2 beyond timing): last_is a2S2u x episode ramp alone gives about 0.10-0.24 on dev; adding trial-before reward gives 0.24 on test; adding the moderate-a2 policy terms gives 0.31 dev / 0.29 test. That is above the additive all-cue ceiling of 0.22 because the terms are multiplicative interactions. No future variables are used (choice is the model own logit at GO). Much of the variance (about 70%) is still unexplained, mostly per-window amplitude differences among a2 S2 u GO steps.
